The two ends of the coil run down to a ring fitted on an axle, the ring being broken into two halves, and a stationary brush touches the ring on each side. The external circuit joining the two brushes contains an ammeter and no cell.
note: FIGURE NEEDED - printed figure (c) on PDF idx 70 (printed p61); it is printed at the TOP OF THE RIGHT-HAND COLUMN, physically separated from figures (a) and (b) which end the left-hand column. OWNERSHIP ADJUDICATED, not assumed: its label 'c.' is set in 13 pt, matching Q11's 'a.'/'b.' labels exactly, while Q10's 'a.'/'b.' labels are 15 pt; two-column reading order also places it immediately after Q11(b). Against that, it is a line drawing where Q11(a) and (b) are photographs, and Q10's wording ('diagrams') suits it better than Q11's ('figures') - so this is a judgement, and it is recorded here. The figure carries no labels at all; the identification in the model answer rests on the split ring, the two brushes and the ammeter-with-no-cell.

stem: Heat energy is being produced in a resistance in a circuit at the rate of 100 W. The current of 3 A is flowing in the circuit. What must be the value of the resistance?
Two tungsten bulbs of wattage 100 W and 60 W power work on 220 V potential difference. If they are connected in parallel, how much current will flow in the main conductor?
note: The printed answer is (Ans : 0.72A). The exact value is 160/220 = 8/11 = 0.7272... A, so the correctly rounded two-decimal figure is 0.73 A; the book's 0.72 A is that value truncated rather than rounded. Recorded in the solution.
